newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares lifted higher by Wall Street rally.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares lifted higher by Wall Street rally.

text.p: Italy stocks were lifted higher in afternoon trade to close higher helped by a rally on Wall Street and supported by firmer domestic bonds, dealers said.
* "The market took its direction from the early rally in the U.S. and soon reversed early losses," one trader said.

* Stocks were little affected by results of Italian local elections, in which the ruling centre-left won four and the centre-right opposition four of the 10 cities where elections were held, and had drifted lower early in quiet trade.
* Blue-chip Mib30 index ended up 0.76 percent at 18,391 while all-share Mibtel was 0.56 percent higher at 12,314.

* Market taking support from Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi stressing in Brussels that Italy would reduce its budget deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997, and reduce it below that level in 1998, dealers said.
* On individual shares, Pirelli up 1.46 percent at 3,898 lire as chairman tells annual shareholders meeting that results from the first four months of 1997 were in line with 1996.

* Generali ends 1.29 percent firmer at 29,756 lire ahead of the group's results issued after the market had closed which showed the group's consolidated net profits up at 1.44 trillion lire from 695 billion lire in 1995 helped by the sale of its stake in French insurer AXA.
* Oil giant ENI ends up 1.27 percent, but industrial group Fiat off 0.02 percent at 5,717 lire and information technology group Olivetti down 0.89 percent at 490 lire.
